dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Rosa. Buenos días, or buenas tardes I guess, it just turned noon. How can I help you?
Yes, hello. Good afternoon. My name is Daniela Herrera. I'm calling about a noise problem and I, um, I wrote some things down so I don't forget. Hold on, let me find my place.
Take your time.
Okay. Here. There is a rental house on my street, and they have a loud party. Music, shouting, people in the yard. Last night it went until two in the morning. Two! I looked at the clock.
Last night, so Sunday into Monday. Is this the first time?

No, no. It has been going on since last Thursday. I have it here. Thursday, loud until maybe midnight. Friday, the storm, you would think nobody goes out, and still they had people there. Saturday, same, with the wind and everything. Then last night, the worst.
Yeah, with the coastal storm Friday and Saturday, I'd think people would stay in. Do you know who owns the house, or who's renting?
I do not know. It changes. Different cars every few months. [pause] Sorry, I am looking at my paper. I did not write the owner, only the dates.
That's okay. Can I get your street, or the house number of the rental?
I would rather not give my street on the phone. I only want to know where this complaint goes. Is that a problem?
No problem for a general question. I just can't pass along a specific complaint about a house without a location, but I can tell you how it works.
Okay. So my question is this. Should I be calling the police? The non-emergency line, I mean. Instead of you. Because at two in the morning, you are closed, and I do not want to call 911 for music.

Right, that's the thing. For a party that's going on right now, the police non-emergency line is the one to use, because they can actually send someone while it's happening. We're not open at night. If you call us, it's more for the pattern afterward, so there's a record.
Hmm. So they come, and they tell them to be quiet.
Usually an officer goes by, talks to them, and can follow up if it keeps happening. And if you call each night, that builds a record of the dates and times too.

I see. It is just annoying. I am seventy-something, I should not have to be up at two in the morning with a pillow on my head. And the street is so quiet otherwise. It is an old street. We have the old stone walls all along, they are older than the country, you know. Those walls have seen centuries and now they have to listen to this.

They really have, a lot of Newport is like that. Well, let me do this. I can take down your name and a note about the dates, and if you want to give me the address later, that can go to whoever handles rental complaints. Would that help?
Yes, write the dates. Thursday the eighth, Friday the ninth, Saturday the tenth, Sunday the eleventh.
Let me check that. Thursday the eighth, Friday the ninth, Saturday the tenth, Sunday the eleventh into Monday. Got it. And a callback number, in case someone wants to follow up?
Yes. It is four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-five-zero.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-five-zero. Perfect. If you decide you want the house on the record, call back with the number and I'll attach it.
All right. I will see what the police say tonight, if they start again. I am not hopeful, but fine.
I hear you. Hopefully it's a quiet one. Gracias for calling, Mrs. Herrera.
Thank you. Goodbye.
